newsitem.title: USA: Instant checks for gun buyers on schedule-Reno.
newsitem.headline: Instant checks for gun buyers on schedule-Reno.

text.p: A national system to check instantly the backgrounds of would-be handgun buyers will be ready by November 1998 and will cover a significant part of the population, Attorney General Janet Reno said on Thursday.

"The FBI is ... even a little ahead of schedule in developing the technical apparatus necessary for the sophisticated computer system that can link the state criminal history records of all the states and provide for an access point so gun dealers (can) get the instant check," she said.
Reno told her weekly news conference the Justice Department wanted the state criminal history records to be as complete as possible when the new system takes effect.

The Supreme Court last week by a 5-4 vote struck down one part of the historic Brady gun control law requiring that local sheriffs conduct the background checks on prospective handgun buyers during a five-day period.
Reno said law enforcement officers she has talked to plan to continue performing the checks voluntarily. "So I don't see significant practical differences (after the ruling)."

In 1995 about 33 percent of state records were complete, up from 18 percent three years earlier, she said. She declined to predict what the percentage would be in 1998 but said she did not know if the records would be totally complete.

"The system will be in place and we will continue to build and to work with the states that don't have complete records, but for a significant part of the population we will be able to provide that instant check," she said.
